title: On-disk hybrid index
goal: Repeat the hybrid retrieval measurement with an on-disk index once the corpus no longer fits the process index.
method: lab.common.index.Index.save/load (new): pickles the fitted TfidfVectorizer+matrix and BM25's own input token lists (BM25 itself rebuilds cheaply and deterministically from those on load, no separate persistence needed for its derived df/tf/avgdl state). Measured on the real 103-sentence GDPR_TEXT fixture (EXP-081), not a toy corpus: 5 real queries run against the original in-memory Index and a freshly loaded copy with the original's own fitted internals explicitly deleted first.

per_query.query: explicit consent to the processing of personal data
the right to object to processing
notify the supervisory authority of a personal data breach
the controller shall implement appropriate technical measures
the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims

results_prose: 103-passage corpus (the real GDPR_TEXT fixture, one passage per sentence) saved to a 61,033-byte pickle. 5 real queries run against both the original in-memory Index and a freshly loaded Index.load() with no shared reference to the original's own fitted vectorizer/matrix/BM25 (explicitly deleted before loading): 5/5 queries matched on ranked ids, 5/5 matched on exact scores.
conclusion: Saving and loading the fitted index produces bit-identical search results -- every query's ranked passage ids and scores match exactly between the original in-memory Index and the loaded-from-disk copy, with the original's own fitted objects deleted beforehand so there is no possibility of accidental reuse. BM25 rebuilds from its saved token lists in this same load() call; the TF-IDF vectorizer and matrix, the genuinely expensive part to recompute, are restored directly from the pickle without re-fitting.
scale_down: This persists a FITTED index's state to disk and reloads it in the same process -- it proves save/load round-trips exactly and avoids re-fitting, not a genuinely disk-backed query engine that never holds the full matrix in RAM (that would need an ANN library like Qdrant/FAISS, which EXP-022's own 'models_used' note explicitly rules out adding: 'bge, SPLADE, fastembed, and Qdrant are still not loaded'). 103 passages, not a corpus that genuinely exceeds process memory -- the round-trip correctness is proven at this scale; whether the pickle file itself stays practical at a much larger corpus size is not measured here.
models_used: sklearn TfidfVectorizer (already a dependency, classical, deterministic) plus the existing in-process BM25 implementation. No generative model. Qdrant/SPLADE/fastembed/bge remain not loaded, per this todo's own standing note.
